name: rcossin_tbl
evidence: RotMatrix, RotMatrix_gte, RotMatrixZYX_gte and RotMatrixYXZ_gte (text_063f04.s) all index it as ((|angle| & 0xFFF) << 2): a word whose low half is sin and high half cos, the sine negated for a negative angle. The native ports read it in place and reproduce the town-map camera and the card-viewer turn.
notes: 4096 {sin, cos} pairs of 1.3.12 shorts. rcossin_tbl is the Psy-Q LIBGTE name for this table; the name is inferred from the library, the layout is verified.

name: gPsyq_awSinQuarterTable
evidence: sin_1 (0x800866E4) reads halfwords at index a for a <= 0x400, 0x800 - a up to 0x800, and the negated mirror above; rsin and rcos call sin_1 after masking to 0xFFF. sin_1 addresses the third quadrant through 0x80093938 + 2a, which is this table at index a - 0x800.
notes: Quarter wave of sine, 0x401 halfwords. Distinct from rcossin_tbl: rsin/rcos use this one, the matrix builders the other.

name: gPsyq_awSquareRootTable
evidence: SquareRoot0 (0x80086E5C) normalizes its argument with the GTE leading-zero counter, indexes this table with ((normalized - 0x40) << 1) and shifts the entry by (31 - even_zero_count) >> 1, then >> 12. GsSetRefView2 and GsSetFlatLight vector lengths come out right through the native port (view test: reference point lands on the view axis at the true distance).
notes: 192 halfword entries for normalized inputs 0x40..0xFF.

name: GsWSMATRIX
evidence: GsSetRefView2 (0x8008AD50) builds the view matrix here from GsIDMATRIX2, the twist and the two axis rotations, stores the translated viewpoint in its t[], and returns 0; GsGetLsUnit and GsGetLwsUnit finish with GsMulCoord2(this, m).
notes: World-to-screen matrix. The existing map row for Model_GetLightSourceMatrix (0x80059220) describes the same address as a light-source matrix: by this evidence it is the view matrix, and that row's note should be revisited.

name: GsLIGHTWSMATRIX
evidence: The last thing GsSetRefView2 does on success is copy the eight words of 0x800FE148 here.
notes: Copy of the world-screen matrix kept for lighting.

name: GsIDMATRIX
evidence: Gssub_make_matrix (0x80086210) copies it into its output before writing one axis rotation's sine and cosine, i.e. it is the identity the rotation is laid over.
notes: Identity matrix.

name: GsIDMATRIX2
evidence: GsSetRefView2 initializes the world-screen matrix from it before any rotation is applied.
notes: Identity matrix used as the view's starting point (aspect-corrected identity in LIBGS).

name: gGs_LightDirectionMatrix
evidence: GsSetFlatLight (0x800857F0) writes row `id` with the normalized, negated light vector ((-v << 12) / |v|) and stores the matrix back; GsSetLightMatrix (0x80085600) copies it, multiplies it by the caller's local-world matrix between PushMatrix/PopMatrix and passes the product to SetLightMatrix.
notes: Three parallel-light directions in world space, one per row.

name: GsOUT_PACKET_P
evidence: GsSetWorkBase stores its argument here; GsScanUnit and GsSortUnit copy it into the driver scratch area (+0x10) and GsSortUnit refreshes that copy after every primitive driver returns; the resident DivideFT4 caller (display_object_helpers.c) passes it as the packet cursor and stores DivideFT4's return value back.
notes: LIBGS output packet cursor.

name: PSDCNT
evidence: GsGetLwUnit, GsGetLsUnit and GsGetLwsUnit compare each coordinate's flg word with it to decide whether workm is already this frame's, and stamp flg with it after computing; libgs.c's GsSwapDispBuff port increments it and skips zero.
notes: LIBGS frame counter used as the coordinate-cache stamp.

name: gGs_apCoordWalkStack
evidence: GsGetLwUnit/GsGetLsUnit/GsGetLwsUnit store each visited coordinate at [depth] on the way up to the root and read [depth - 1] back while multiplying down (the code addresses the read side as 0x800FE274 + depth * 4).
notes: Coordinate hierarchy walk stack.

name: gGs_pScanNextBlock
evidence: GsScanUnit (0x80089F80) loads it from word 0 of the primitive block on the priming call and follows it when the per-block count runs out; 0xFFFFFFFF ends the scan.
notes: GsScanUnit state: next primitive block.

name: gGs_pScanCursor
evidence: GsScanUnit sets it past the three-word block header, reports *cursor as the type word, and advances it by one word plus the low half of word 1.
notes: GsScanUnit state: current type word.

name: gGs_pScanPrimHeader
evidence: GsScanUnit loads it from word 1 of each block and copies its section pointers into the scratch area; GsGetHeadpUnit (0x8008A138) returns it and GsMapCoordUnit takes the coordinate section from its last entry.
notes: GsScanUnit state: primitive header (section table) of the current block.

name: gGs_wScanTypesLeft
evidence: GsScanUnit loads it from the low half of word 2 of each block, decrements it per call and moves to the next block when it goes negative.
notes: GsScanUnit state: type words left in the block.

name: lDivideFT4_EmitPacket
evidence: Called four times by RCpolyFT4A (0x80089488) at the last division level with the corner pointers in t0-t3: writes a POLY_FT4 (colour word from DIVPOLYGON4+0x10, the four sxy and uv words, clut and tpage from +0xC/+0xE into the first two uv words), links it at the head of the ordering-table entry at +0x14 with length 9, and advances the packet pointer by 0x28. The native port built from this reading draws the card viewer's card correctly.
notes: Leaf emitter of the FT4 subdivision; register-argument internal routine, not a C-callable function.

name: DisplayObject_ProjectFacing
evidence: Sets the geometry offset and screen, builds the object's Z-Y-X rotation from field_20..22 (RotMatrixZYX_gte), scales by field_44/46 unless GsROTOFF, and takes the NCLIP sign of a unit triangle (RotAverageNclip3_nom, gte_stopz). When field_10 is a callback it is called with that sign, and for a back-facing object the matrix's x and z columns are negated and the test repeated. With the callback never run (pointer-sign test on a host) the card viewer kept the front texture while showing the back; with it run, the back texture appears for the first half of the turn.
notes: Chooses the visible face of a rotating display object. DisplayObject.field_10 is a face-change callback (CardPreview_UpdateVariant, DisplayObject_SetResourceVariantFromSign) or a small number; retail tells them apart by the sign of the word.

name: gPsyq_awArcTangentTable
evidence: ratan2 (0x800899A0) divides the smaller of |x| and |y| by the larger scaled to 0..1024 and reads a halfword here; for |y| >= |x| it uses 0x400 minus the entry, then mirrors by the signs (0x800 - a for negative x, negation for negative y).
notes: atan(n / 1024) for n = 0..1024 in 4096ths of a turn.

name: gGs_dwScanAnimTypesLeft
evidence: GsScanAnim (0x80089D30) loads it from the first word of the type table with the top bit cleared on the priming call, returns 0 when it reaches zero and decrements it per reported type.
notes: GsScanAnim state.

name: gGs_pScanAnimTypeTable
evidence: GsScanAnim's priming call stores the pointer found at word 2 of the block whose address sits two words before its argument.
notes: GsScanAnim state: interpolation-driver type table.

name: gGs_pScanAnimCursor
evidence: GsScanAnim reports *cursor and its address through the GsTYPEUNIT argument and advances it one word per call.
notes: GsScanAnim state.

name: ViewState.pitch
evidence: The second orbit angle in ViewState_ApplyOrbit, in the game's 4096-unit turn. Watched live in the duel: 256 (22.5 degrees above the mat) for the view the duel is played from, tweening to 1022 (level with the mat) for the zone picker, the card-use view and the guardian-star presentation. func_800178BC sets that 0x3FE itself.

name: ModelSlot.stance
evidence: Model_LoadMonsterMerge copies its p4 argument here and then passes it as FileTransferDescriptor.position, which func_80056D7C reads as its `alternate` selector: phases 4 and 6 upload one of two texture sets and phases 7-10 copy one of two variant modules from it. func_800559D4 also compares field_BF5 with field_DFE + 3.

name: ModelSlot.quiet_load
evidence: Set from bit 0x80 of Model_LoadMonsterMerge's slot argument. func_80056D7C skips the sequence-bank sector (phase 13) and the 50-sector voice block (phase 14) when it is set and leaves the three control-module command words at field_CF8+0x10 as -1; func_80056828 then skips the sound bank, and both module dispatchers skip a negative command.
notes: model.h calls it field_E1D. The port's field models load with it set, which is why they need no per-monster module (src/pc/mods/field_models.c).

name: Duel_DrawFieldCard
evidence: Draws one field card: four corners through RotTransSV and RotColorDpq, then GsSortPoly into D_800E9D90[2] at (sum of the four depths)/4 >> 2 -- a sixteenth of the distance, where a model's primitives sort at a quarter of theirs. The port quarters the GTE Z factors for its field models to put the two on one scale.
notes: Already named in the tree as func_80015EF4; the depth scale is what the port measured.

name: gDuel_bBattleUse3DPresentation
evidence: DuelScene_UpdateFieldActions (0x8001D670) clears it at the attack-target step and sets it to 1 only when the confirming press is the game's 0x80 bit (Square: the pad word the game reads is byte-swapped relative to the raw pad, so 0xC0 there is Cross|Square); DuelScene_UpdateBattle (0x8001F55C) then takes state 5, which fills D_800EF658's two AnimatedBattleModelProperties and starts the model scene, instead of state 7, the card clash with effect 2. Reproduced in the PC port from slot1.state: Square on the target gave the 3D arena battle, Cross the card clash.
notes: Byte flag. Name inferred from the behaviour; the flag is verified.

name: gText_adwGlyphCodeTable
evidence: Text_SjisToGlyphCodes (0x8003BC40) scans u32 words from index 1 until a zero word and emits the index whose low halfword equals the Shift-JIS code it was given. Read from the verified SLUS: 91 entries after the unused word 0, the low halves being full-width Latin letters, digits and punctuation (0x8285 'e' first, then by frequency); glyph 0 is the space. Decoding card 1's name through it gives 'Blue-eyes White Dragon' and card 58's 'Kuriboh'; the port's card names (src/pc/cards/cards.c) are encoded through it and drawn by the game.
notes: u32 per glyph code, Shift-JIS in the low half. notes/card-catalog.md already names it gText_adwGlyphCodeTable.

name: gLibrary_szCountHeading
evidence: Entry 0xF8 of the D_801C0000 offset table is 0x121D, and func_8002BFCC (library_runtime.c) builds its heading with TextBox_Create(3, 0xF8, ...). The bytes are glyph '<', F8 03 with the address 0x801D5608 and width byte 0x83 (func_80038148 prints D_801D5608[0].library_count as three zero-padded digits), then '/722>' and 0xFF. The string ends at 0x801B122A, one byte before D_801B122B. The port's replacement for more cards is drawn in its place.
notes: The Library's '<seen/722>' heading. The name is inferred from what it says; the bytes and the lookup are verified.
